nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
لِإِيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ (1): the position of al-Akhfash is that the meaning is: He did that to them (the People of the Elephant) in order to bring Quraysh together in familiarity.
The error in this view is evident: if it were as he said, لإيلاف would be one of the verses of «ألم تر» (Sūrat al-Fīl), and in the consensus of the Muslims on separating them there is what indicates otherwise than what he said. Also, if it were as he said, the end of the (preceding) sūra would not be complete, and this is not found in any of the sūras. It has been said that there is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "Marvel at the familiarity (īlāf) of Quraysh — رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ — and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House". This, I mean the omission, is the position of al-Farrāʾ, and it is argued for on the basis that the Arabs say لله أبوك ("to Allah [belongs] your father!"), so that the lām carries the sense of wonder. More correct than these two views — and it is the view of al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad — is that the meaning is: "for Allah's bringing Quraysh together in familiarity".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
I.e., for this, let them worship Him. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is no omission, and it is among the fine and subtle points of grammar, even though the authors of the books of Maʿānī overlooked it. «إلفهم» (i.e., إِيلافِهِمْ) is genitive as a badal (substitute), as you say: عجبت من إحسانك إحسانك إلى زيد ("I marvelled at your kindness — your kindness to Zayd"): you substitute the second for the first and add to the information for clarification. It is narrated from Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ that he read «إلفهم», and «إلافهم» is also narrated from him; they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of alifa yaʾlafu, on the patterns fiʿl and fiʿāl. Fiʿl is like their saying ḥalama ḥilman, ʿalima ʿilman and sakhira sikhran; and fiʿāl is like laqītuhu liqāʾan, ṣumtu ṣiyāman and katabtu kitāban. Al-Farrāʾ permitted لِإِيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ إِيلافِهِمْ as a maṣdar [Translator's note: the context implies the accusative, إِيلافَهُمْ, though the printed vowelling shows the genitive]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The accusative is also permissible in إلفهم and إيلافهم, in the sense of "they become familiar with a familiarity". رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ is accusative by إيلاف; and al-Farrāʾ permitted إيلافهم رحلةِ الشتاء والصّيف (in the genitive). Abū Jaʿfar said: This would be by way of badal, its implied form being: "their familiarity, the familiarity with the journey of winter and summer".
فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هذَا الْبَيْتِ (3): and if you wish, you may give the lām kasra according to its origin.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ربّ; it may also be in the position of the nominative, i.e., "He is the One who". أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, and وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ is included in the ṣila.
